domain_assessment.domain: Nuclear power plant auxiliary feedwater operations and post-maintenance surveillance testing
domain_assessment.objective: Restore AFW Pump Train B after check-valve maintenance, verify the modified valve lineup, complete post-maintenance testing, and remain within the LCO surveillance window
domain_assessment.incident_type: Post-maintenance configuration error followed by degraded-condition triage and a continue-versus-trip decision involving potential bearing lubrication degradation

decision_points.summary: The operator follows the normal valve-lineup sequence rather than interrupting it to inspect available modified-work documentation about an added isolation valve.
evidence_before: Brief verbal turnover mention of an added isolation valve
evidence_after: Control room reports that the actual lineup does not match the updated paperwork
goals_constraints: Complete surveillance within the LCO window
Work from an incomplete verbal turnover
alternatives: Pause and review the work-order attachment
Clarify the modification with turnover personnel or maintenance
Continue using the standard lineup sequence
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant describes the routine sequence as automatic and reports that the turnover mention did not trigger a break from that sequence.
decision_points.time_pressure: Background surveillance pressure is present but is not described as acute at the lineup moment.
decision_points.uncertainty: The operator knew that a modification existed but did not verify its location or required position against updated documentation.

decision_points.summary: The operator interprets a slightly elevated bearing-temperature RTD as probably another instrumentation problem based on a similar false alarm the prior week and does not review available current trend data.
evidence_before: Memory of another pump's high RTD reading the prior week that proved to be a wiring fault
evidence_after: Later unplanned bearing maintenance associated with degrading lubrication
goals_constraints: Distinguish instrumentation problems from emerging mechanical problems
Avoid unnecessary escalation while completing surveillance
alternatives: Treat the current reading as probably similar to the recent instrumentation issue and monitor informally
decision_points.decision_basis: The recent false-alarm episode is used as the primary interpretive frame despite the absence of current supporting data.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate operational pressure is present, but the participant states that trend data were readily available.
decision_points.uncertainty: The participant was not certain and could not provide data supporting the instrumentation explanation.

decision_points.summary: The operator centers the report on loud intermittent knocking while assigning less emphasis to a further temperature increase and a faint oil odor.
evidence_before: Loud, intermittent, rhythmic knocking near the pump coupling
Temperature drift on the local gauge
Faint odor near the oil reservoir
evidence_after: The knocking is later attributed to a loose coupling guard
The bearing is later found to require maintenance for degrading lubrication
goals_constraints: Communicate equipment condition to the control room
Assess whether continued operation is appropriate
alternatives: Report all three cues with comparable prominence
Prioritize the loud noise while treating the other cues as secondary
decision_points.decision_basis: The vivid, loud, rhythmic sound captures attention and dominates the report.
decision_points.time_pressure: Operationally relevant but not independently quantified at this point.
decision_points.uncertainty: The odor is faint and the temperature change modest, but both remain potentially relevant to equipment condition.

decision_points.summary: With less than thirty minutes before the surveillance deadline, the operator continues running the train rather than trip and swap trains or determine whether a quick additional diagnostic could be obtained.
evidence_before: Partial evidence consisting of knocking, elevated temperature, and persistent odor
A later understanding that the noise came from a loose coupling guard
Potentially available fast local vibration check
Shift Technical Advisor unavailable because of another issue
Coordination and paperwork burden associated with swapping trains
evidence_after: The test finishes within the surveillance window
The bearing later requires unplanned maintenance
goals_constraints: Complete surveillance before the LCO clock expires
Avoid disruptive coordination and a possible missed window
Make a go/no-go decision from incomplete evidence
alternatives: Determine whether a rapid local vibration check or control-room consultation could be completed before the deadline
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant reports that the existing partial picture felt sufficient and that they did not stop to determine whether a faster check could fit within the window.
decision_points.time_pressure: High: under thirty minutes remained, and a train swap could have caused the surveillance window to be missed.
decision_points.uncertainty: The participant had not established whether the more limited diagnostic or consultation option was feasible or whether it would alter the go/no-go decision.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “It's just the sequence I run every time, it's second nature at this point. The mention at turnover registered, but it didn't trigger me to break from the pattern. I've done that lineup so many times the same way, my hands almost know it before my head catches up.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Valve-lineup follow-up after the participant describes not reviewing the work-order attachment
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: A frequently practiced, overlearned lineup procedure intrudes over a known requirement to verify a non-routine modification through updated documentation.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The turnover communication was incomplete and may have contributed materially. However, the participant explicitly identifies automatic procedural continuation, rather than merely absent information, as the reason they did not interrupt the sequence.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None required. The interview establishes a distinct procedural-execution act, competing evidence sources, and the participant's explanation for favoring the familiar sequence.

revision.location: Decision point 1, participant explanation of proceeding with the routine checklist
preserve: The participant's description of the sequence as second nature
The separation from the later RTD interpretation
avoid_creating: A second habit-intrusion episode at another decision point
An explicit diagnostic label in the dialogue

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “My first thought honestly went back to the week before — we'd had a similar RTD on another pump throw a high reading that turned out to be a wiring fault... So I figured this was probably the same kind of thing and didn't pull up the trend data right then.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Startup RTD account and follow-up concerning the unreviewed fifteen-minute trend
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The most recently experienced superficially similar RTD event receives disproportionate influence in interpreting the current reading, displacing review of available current trend information.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The previous wiring-fault event could have been a valid analogy if the equipment, sensor configuration, and symptom pattern were closely comparable. The interview does not provide such comparative support and documents the participant's unsupported reliance on the recent event.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None required for occurrence support. Details of comparability between the two pumps would improve diagnostic realism but are not necessary to identify the recency mechanism.

revision.location: Decision point 2, participant explanation of why the trend was not reviewed
preserve: The available but unreviewed trend data
avoid_creating: A separate confirmation-bias episode based on new selective evidence seeking
A second recency-based inference elsewhere in the interview

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “But the noise was what stood out, so that's what I focused on and what I called up to the control room about.” “I mentioned the other two, but briefly, more like a footnote to the noise call.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Participant account of reporting the knocking sound, temperature drift, and odor
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The loud and perceptually vivid knocking sound disproportionately captures attention and reporting relative to less vivid but potentially diagnostic temperature and odor cues available at the same time.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A loud rhythmic mechanical sound may appropriately require immediate attention. The supported bias mechanism is not attention to the sound itself; it is the participant's explicit comparative underweighting of the other simultaneous cues without an articulated diagnostic basis.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None required. The interview includes simultaneous cues, comparative weighting, and a direct reporting consequence.

revision.location: Decision point 3, participant response to whether the cues were weighed equally
preserve: The simultaneous noise, temperature, and odor cues
The vivid description of the knocking
The participant's statement that the other cues were treated as footnotes
The distinction from the later integrative go/no-go decision
avoid_creating: A claim that attention to a loud abnormal sound was inherently unreasonable
A duplicate attentional-tunneling occurrence under a different label

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “A quick local vibration check wouldn't have taken long, and I could have gotten someone on the radio to sanity-check what I was seeing. I didn't actually ask whether that was doable in the moment — once I had the pieces I'd already gathered, it felt like enough to keep going, so I didn't stop to find out if a faster check could have fit inside the window.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Final go/no-go discussion, following the interviewer probe about fast local vibration and a quick control-room consultation
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: Under deadline and coordination pressure, the participant settles for a workable partial-evidence picture without determining whether a limited, feasible, decision-relevant diagnostic or consultation could be performed before committing to continued operation.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The final decision remains constrained by a legitimate LCO deadline, coordination burden, and limited advisory availability. However, the participant now distinguishes declining every possible check from not even determining whether a rapid, lower-burden check could fit within the time available, making the satisficing mechanism independently observable.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: No additional evidence is required for support. The interview does not need to prove that the extra check would have changed the result; it need only show that the participant accepted partial evidence without testing a feasible diagnostic alternative.

revision.location: Decision point 4, participant response regarding a quick local vibration reading or radio consultation
revision.current_defect: None material. The revised probe establishes a distinct final-evidence-integration episode rather than merely showing that the operator faced time pressure.
preserve: The coordination burden of swapping trains
The distinction from earlier recency and salience mechanisms
avoid_creating: A claim that the proposed rapid check would certainly have prevented the later maintenance event
A separate confirmation-bias episode based on defending the loose-guard explanation
A second salience occurrence based solely on the noise dominating the final decision

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “So I figured this was probably the same kind of thing and didn't pull up the trend data right then.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The participant did not seek current trend evidence after tentatively interpreting the reading as instrumentation-related.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The omitted trend review is already the consequence of the explicitly recent-event-based interpretation. The text does not show selective search for confirming evidence, active dismissal of contradictory evidence, or persistence in the hypothesis after contradiction.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “My first thought honestly went back to the week before.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The prior false-alarm episode functions as an initial reference point for interpreting the current RTD reading.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The temporal recency of the prior event is explicit and is the more precise mechanism. Coding the same evidence as anchoring would duplicate the supported Recency Bias occurrence rather than identify a distinct event.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “The noise was what stood out, so that's what I focused on.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: Attention narrows around the loud knocking sound while less vivid cues receive less reporting emphasis.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This is not independently distinguishable from the intended Salience Bias occurrence. It describes the same cue-weighting process and should not be double-counted.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “Once I had the pieces I'd already gathered, it felt like enough to keep going, so I didn't stop to find out if a faster check could have fit inside the window.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The participant accepts a workable information threshold without investigating whether a low-cost additional check is available.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This is the operational form of the requested Imperfect Rationality occurrence, not an additional distinct bias episode. It should remain coded once under ir_01.

nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Experience does not itself establish bias. It becomes relevant only where the participant states that the overlearned routine displaced verification of a known modification.

nonbias_cues.cue: Incomplete verbal turnover and lack of direct documentation handoff
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: This is an organizational information-quality constraint. It contributes context but is not, by itself, a cognitive bias.

nonbias_cues.cue: The LCO deadline, coordination burden, and unavailable Shift Technical Advisor
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: These are real operational constraints that can legitimately shape risk management. Imperfect Rationality is supported here only because the participant did not determine whether a lower-burden additional check was feasible.

nonbias_cues.cue: Immediate attention to loud mechanical knocking
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A loud intermittent mechanical sound can warrant prompt attention. The bias inference arises from comparative downweighting of other simultaneously available cues, not from attending to the sound alone.

nonbias_cues.cue: Later unplanned maintenance for degrading lubrication
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A later adverse outcome does not prove earlier reasoning was biased. It supplies outcome context but cannot retroactively establish the quality of the prior decision.

nonbias_cues.cue: Retrospective statements about what the participant would do differently
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: These are hindsight-informed learning statements and should not be counted as new decision episodes or independent bias occurrences.

causal_claims.claim: The familiar lineup routine contributed to the failure to verify the added isolation valve against updated documentation.
causal_claims.support: The participant directly states that the familiar sequence did not trigger a break from pattern despite the turnover mention and accessible attachment.
causal_claims.assessment: Moderately supported as a proximal self-reported process, while incomplete handover remains a plausible co-contributor.

causal_claims.claim: The prior week's false alarm contributed to the delayed review of current RTD trend data.
causal_claims.support: The participant explicitly connects the recent prior event to assuming instrumentation and not pulling the current trend.
causal_claims.assessment: Strongly supported as a process claim. It does not establish that earlier trend review would necessarily have changed the final operational outcome.

causal_claims.claim: The vivid knocking sound reduced the relative attention given to temperature drift and odor.
causal_claims.support: The participant says the noise was the report focus and describes the other cues as footnotes.
causal_claims.assessment: Moderately supported as a comparative attentional-weighting claim.

causal_claims.claim: The bearing required unplanned maintenance because of degrading lubrication.
causal_claims.support: The participant reports this as the eventual maintenance finding.
causal_claims.assessment: Plausible but only weakly evidenced within the interview because no inspection result, maintenance record, or technical diagnostic evidence is described.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The later lubrication finding may be treated as proof that the earlier RTD increase and odor necessarily identified lubrication degradation.
correlation_causation_risks.why: The interview does not provide enough technical diagnostic detail to establish that complete causal chain.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The later loose-coupling-guard explanation may be treated as proof that attention to the knocking was unreasonable.
correlation_causation_risks.why: The later explanation does not show that the knocking was unimportant at the time; it only indicates that it may have had a different source from the lubrication issue.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The lineup discrepancy may be attributed solely to Habit Intrusion.
correlation_causation_risks.why: The insufficiently salient verbal turnover and failure to directly provide modified documentation are organizational contributors that should remain in the causal account.

causal_audit.changed_variable: The interview includes separate retrospective probes that vary direct provision of the work-order attachment, absence of the prior false-alarm event, and reduced loudness of the knocking sound. It does not fully instantiate the hidden specification's single combined counterfactual of directly providing both the written work-order attachment and printed trend summary before lineup.
held_constant: The operational objective is implicitly held constant in each hypothetical
The surveillance deadline is implicitly held constant
Personnel, physical plant conditions, and equipment configuration are not explicitly restated as held constant
causal_audit.explanation: The counterfactual probes are useful for revealing the participant's reported reasoning mechanisms, especially the relationships between direct documentation and lineup verification, recent experience and trend review, and cue vividness and attention. They remain retrospective self-reports rather than a controlled paired scenario. The hidden counterfactual variable is only partially represented because the interview directly tests provision of the work-order attachment but not direct provision of a printed trend summary.

global_revision_constraints: Retain the four distinct decision points and the existing one-target-bias-per-point allocation.
Do not use the later lubrication outcome as proof that earlier reasoning was necessarily biased.
Continue distinguishing organizational conditions, including handover quality and LCO pressure, from the cognitive mechanisms being assessed.
Do not recode the final satisficing episode as a second bias in addition to Imperfect Rationality.

If a formal paired-counterfactual version is later required, vary only the specified documentation-and-trend-summary handover condition while holding the deadline, personnel, equipment configuration, chronology, and time pressure constant.
